column1: # docs/project/tickets.tsv — THE TICKET INDEX. Every bug, cosmetic item and
# evolution of this project, one row per GitHub issue. THE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR
# THE LIST (CLAUDE.md [VSP-182], maintainer-ruled 2026-09-14), and this header is
# its spec of record. docs/project/tickets.md is GENERATED from it
# (`python3 tools/tickets.py page`); the gate is tests/test_tickets.sh.
# ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH PER QUESTION:
#   the LIST — which tickets exist, their kind and status ...... this file
#   the STORY — report, discussion, rulings as given, resolution  the GitHub issue
#   the FACTS a ticket established .............................. the subject documents ([VSP-12])
#   what a SESSION did .......................................... STATE.md / STATE_HISTORY.md ([VSP-17])
# Live documents name a ticket by its issue number (#N) and never restate its
# status or content. A copy of past content names its origin and date, and goes
# only into a source of truth or an archive.
# ENOUGH STAYS LOCAL: without GitHub, the tree must answer four questions about
# every ticket — the four answer columns below. Only the conversation, and a
# third party's report text, may exist on GitHub alone.
# repo: DefinitelyFrenchName/VampireSaved
# COLUMNS (tab-separated; rows ordered newest issue first):
#   issue     the GitHub issue number, the key. Every issue on GitHub has exactly
#             one row; a ticket with no issue yet does not exist yet.
#   kind      bug | cosmetic | evolution. A change of kind is an edit here and a
#             label on GitHub, never a move.
#               bug        a defect: something does not do what it should
#               cosmetic   presentation only, no gameplay effect
#               evolution  a change or capability to add, not a defect
#   status    open | parked                                   the issue is OPEN
#             done | declined | not-ours | invalid | duplicate  the issue is CLOSED
#               done       fixed, or delivered
#               declined   ruled not to be done
#               not-ours   vanilla behaviour, or outside this project
#               invalid    the premise was refuted
#               duplicate  another ticket holds it (named in `decided`)
#             CLOSED MEANS NOTHING IS LEFT TO DO: an option kept open is its own
#             ticket, linked from this one.
#             GitHub's close reason (completed / not planned) is not mapped:
#             the status is this column's.
#   title     one searchable line, in our words
#   repro     how to reproduce it: a recording, a replay, a rig or a gate
#   decided   what was decided. Rulings are recorded locally whatever channel
#             gave them: STATE "Standing rulings", DECISIONS_HISTORY.md, a doc.
#   learned   what was learned: the mechanism, the measurement
#   wrong     what went wrong: retracted theories, traps, bad patterns
#             Each answer is `none`, or links separated by ` ; `. A link is a
#             repo-relative `path`, which must exist, or `path § text`, where
#             some line of the file must contain the text. `learned` and `wrong`
#             link a LIVE document (a subject doc, a gotchas bucket, a skill),
#             never STATE.md, which rolls, or an archive (`*_HISTORY.md`,
#             `*_history.md`).
#   sessions  the session keys that worked on it, comma-separated
#             (`14z-112,14z-126b`), each resolving in STATE.md or
#             STATE_HISTORY.md; or `-`
# BACKFILL DEBT: `?` in any column but issue and title marks a row not yet
# backfilled (the retrofit that opened this file, 2026-09-14). Only issues listed
# in tests/expected/tickets_debt.txt may carry `?`, and that list only SHRINKS:
# the commit that answers a row's last `?` removes the issue from it.
# THE GITHUB SIDE: docs/project/tickets_github.tsv is GitHub's issue list as
# saved by `python3 tools/tickets.py refresh` at a session close, and the gate
# compares open/closed against it offline. A NEW TICKET: create the issue,
# refresh, add the row. CLOSING ONE (CLAUDE.md [VSP-182]), in one commit: its
# facts go where they belong; the issue and the tree are reconciled and a closing
# comment states the resolution; this row records the status and the four
# answers; any STATE entry for it moves VERBATIM to STATE_HISTORY.md under the
# closing session's key.
# WHAT THE GATE DOES NOT CLAIM: that an answer is ENOUGH. That is judged at the
# close that closes the ticket.
